_about: Follow-up instructions for the AI, and the fallback template sent when the AI budget is used up or its draft fails the checks. Placeholders: {{first_name}} (or 'there'), {{company}}, {{signal_title}} (the job or launch title, the grounded phrase), {{proof_point}} (the first listed proof point), {{subject}} (the opening email's subject). agent/tests checks every filled template passes the guardrails.

d4_followup_signal2.instructions: A different public signal than the first email used. Two or three sentences, in the same thread.

template.subject: Re: {{subject}}
template.body: Hi {{first_name}}, one more thing I noticed at {{company}}: {{signal_title}}. Would it help to see how a signal like that turns into a first email your team only has to approve?

d4_new_subject.instructions: They didn't engage with the first email. A fresh angle on the same signal with a new subject line, two sentences, low pressure.

template.subject: A quick thought on {{signal_title}}
template.body: Hi {{first_name}}, a short follow-up about {{signal_title}} at {{company}}. {{proof_point}}, so it stays light for a small team. Open to a quick look?

d7_case.instructions: One short note on how the offer works for a team at their stage, using only the listed proof points. Never invent a customer story.

template.subject: Re: {{subject}}
template.body: Hi {{first_name}}, one detail that matters while {{company}} works on {{signal_title}}: {{proof_point}}. Worth a short look this week?

d11_close.instructions: A polite close-the-loop. One or two sentences; make it easy to say not now.

template.subject: Re: {{subject}}
template.body: Hi {{first_name}}, I'll stop following up here. If {{signal_title}} turns into an outbound push later, should I reach back out then?
